content: The purpose of this Operating Instruction is to establish a pre - contract award complaint s procedure for vendors to challenge certain decisions made by NSPA in the context of NSPA procurements. 3. SCOPE This instruction is applicable to all competitive solicitation processes up to contract award and Notifications of Planned Sole Source Award (NPSSA) concerning requirements ≥ 800K € conducted by NSPA . 4. GENERAL PRINCIPLES 4.1 The following principles shall apply to the complaint proce dure : 4.1.1 All complaints and appeals shall be made in good faith. 4.1.2 Complaints and appeals against NSPA decisions and determinations are inadmissible if the bidder was ineligible for the relevant competitive solicitation process. 4.1.3 B reaches or errors that do not materially affect the outcome of the final decision shall not lead to the annulment of said decision. 4.2 Complaints that fail to adhere to any of the principles above shall be dismiss ed as will complaints from bidders that acknowledge non - compliance with any one mandatory requirement . NATO UNCLASSIFIED NSPA OI 4200 - 08 26 June 2025 NATO UNCLASSIFIED - 6 - 5. SUBMISSION OF COMPLAINTS 5.1 Bidders may challenge NSPA decisions for one of the reasons set out i n Paragraph 5.3 below . 5.2 When submitting complaint s , bidders are precluded from correct ing , alter ing , add ing or dele ting any part of the ir bid. 5.3 Groun

PROCEDURE 6.1 Informal Dispute Resolution Be fore submitting the complaint, bidders shall make good faith effort s to resolve amicably the dispute . The start of the info rmal dispute resolution process do es not suspend the time limits for submitting a complaint unless expressly agreed to by the Competition Advocate . 6.2 Timelines The time limit s for filing complaints depend on the d ecision being contested and are provided in P aragraphs 6.2.1 – 6.2.4 b elow . content: nd paragraph number , its factual and regulatory basis, and the alleged violations or irregularities; 6.3.1.3 any other relevant document that substantiates the arguments made in the complaint ; and 6.3.1.4 the remedy sought listed under Paragraph 7 below, including an explicit request that NSPA suspend the procurement process. 6.3.2 The Procurement Officer responsible for the competitive solicitation process must record receipt of the complaint in the NSPA Vendor Complaint Management (VCM) system and update as required throughout the process . 6.4 First - Level Review by the Senior Procurement Officer/Technical Team 6.4.1 The Procurement Officer shall, in consultation with the Technical Team when applicable , examine the complaint within 10 NSPA business days following its receipt and determine whether it warrants an amendment or re - issuance of the RFP or a re - evaluation of the proposal. In exceptional circumstances, the Competition Advocate may seek further information from subject matter experts not involved with the RFP (e.g. technical experts) . 6.5.3 The Competition Advocate shall issue a written decision, stating the ir findings and reasons for the decision, normally within 15 NSPA business days fr o m the receipt of the complaint . 6.6 Appeal Procedure before the NSPA Award Review and Debarment Board 6.6.1 T he bidder may challenge the Competition Advoc ate ’s decision , by refer ring the dispute to the NSPA Award Review and Debarment Board (ARDB) for adjudication . 6.6.2 The adjudication shall be conducted in accordance with the ARDB’s Terms of Reference (Reference E ) . 6.6.3 The decision of the ARDB shall be final. 7. REMEDIES 7.1 Remedies for Complaints for Unduly Restrictive Requirements If the complaint for unduly restrictive requirements pursuant to Paragraph 5.3.1 is we ll - founded, NSPA shall amend the RFPs by removing

folder: NATO Support and Procurement Agency — NSPA
content: 1 Remedies for Complaints for Unduly Restrictive Requirements If the complaint for unduly restrictive requirements pursuant to Paragraph 5.3.1 is we ll - founded, NSPA shall amend the RFPs by removing unduly restrictive specifications or requirements and re - advertise the RFP . NSPA may also discontinue the competitive solicitation process. 7.2 Remedies for Complaints for Determinations of Non - Compliance If the complaint for a determination of non - compliance pursuant to Paragraph 5.3.2 is well - founded, NSPA shall amend the technical evaluation report or conduct a new technical /commercial evaluation . NSPA may also discontinue the competitive solicitation process. 7.3 Remedies for Complaints Relating to Notifications of Planned Sole Source Awards If the complaint for an erroneous determination of the sole source character of a requirement pursuant to Paragraph 5.3. 3 is well - founded, NSPA shall cancel the Notification of Planned Sole Source Awards and issue a competitive RFP. NSPA may also discontinue the process. NATO UNCLASSIFIED NSPA OI 4200 - 08 26 June 2025 NATO UNCLASSIFIED - 9 - 8. INAPPLICABILITY OF REMEDIES DUE TO SECURITY CONCE R N S Notwithstanding P aragraphs 7 .1 to 7 . 3 above , if the remedies could have serious security implications, upon the recommendation of the Gener al Manager, the Competition Advocate may dismiss the complaint. content: .1 to 7 . 3 above , if the remedies could have serious security implications, upon the recommendation of the Gener al Manager, the Competition Advocate may dismiss the complaint. This decision shall not be subject to appeal. 9. ENTRY INTO FORCE This procedure shall enter into force on 2 6 June 2025 . From the effective date, all pre - award complaints submitted to NSPA shall be subject to this procedure. PURPOSE An independent NSPA Award Review and Debarment Board (the “Board”) is established to enhance the trust and confidence of stakeholders in NSPA dec isions regarding source selection and contract awards. The Board is also established to review debarment decisions affecting suppliers alleged to have engaged in sanctionable practices in order to ensure that resources and funds entrusted to NSPA are us ed only for their intended purposes. The Board is competent to hear and make final decisions on appeals on the grounds listed in Paragraph 4.7 below. 3. SCOPE This Operating Instruction contains the rules of procedure applicable to the Board. 4. GOVERNANCE, COMPOSITION AND OPERATION OF THE BOARD 4.1 Composition of the Board and Appointment of Members 4.1.1 The Board shall be composed of five procurement and/or legal experts external to NSPA and appointed by the General Manager (GM) through a competitive selection process. 4.1.2 All members of the Board shall be nationals of NATO Member Nations. 4.1.3 As a transitional measure, the Board may operate with a more limited composition until all five members of the Board have been appointed. 4.1.4 Once all members of the Board are appointed, they shall hold a plenary meeting with the Secretariat and agree on any procedure not provided for under these rules. NATO UNCLASSIFIED NSPA OI 4200-09 18 December 2025 NATO UNCLASSIFIED -

NATO UNCLASSIFIED NSPA OI 4200-09 18 December 2025 NATO UNCLASSIFIED -6- 4.1.5 The Board shall elect one President and one Vice-President. The President and the Vice-President shall be elected for a two-year term that can be renewed for one additional two- year term. 4.1.6 The President of the Board shall declare the opening and closing of each plenary meeting, direct the discussions in plenary meetings, ensure observance of these rules, accord the right to speak, put questions and announce decisions. The President shall rule on points of order and, subject to these rules, shall have complete control of the proceedings at any meeting. 4.1.7 The Vice-President shall act as President where the President is unable to perform their functions. When the Vice-President, acting in replacement of the President, is also unable to perform their own functions, a new officer shall be elected. 4.1.8 NSPA shall equip the Board with a Secretariat. The Secretariat shall be tasked with providing administrative support to the Board and manage the communications between the parties. 4.2 Panel Composition and Venue 4.2.1 All appeals before the Board shall be reviewed by a three-member panel and decided by majority decision. 4.2.2 The Board shall normally hold remote sess

folder: NATO Support and Procurement Agency — NSPA
content: parties. 4.2 Panel Composition and Venue 4.2.1 All appeals before the Board shall be reviewed by a three-member panel and decided by majority decision. 4.2.2 The Board shall normally hold remote sessions and meet by using VTC equipment and facilities. Where in situ meetings are required, the Secretariat of the Board may convene a meeting at NSPA or another suitable location. 4.3 Eligibility for Appointment To be eligible for appointment as a member of the Board, a person shall: 4.3.1 be of high moral character and impartial; 4.3.2 possess at least ten years of experience in the field of public law, international procurement, dispute settlement, arbitration or debarment. 4.3.3 be fluent in English (working knowledge of French is desirable). 4.4 Independence of the Board 4.4.1 A member of the Board shall be appointed for one non-renewable term of six years. 4.4.2 A member of the Board shall not be eligible for any appointment within NSPA for a period of two years following their term of office. 4.4.3 Former NSPA personnel are ineligible to apply for positions until at least two years have lapsed since their departure from NSPA. 4.4.4 Before accepting employment with any entity that has appeared before the Board within two years after separating from service, former Board members shall inform the Board’s Secretariat of their intention in writing, providing all relevant informatio

folder: NATO Support and Procurement Agency — NSPA
content: has appeared before the Board within two years after separating from service, former Board members shall inform the Board’s Secretariat of their intention in writing, providing all relevant information. NATO UNCLASSIFIED NSPA OI 4200-09 18 December 2025 NATO UNCLASSIFIED -7- 4.4.5 A member of the Board shall serve in their personal capacity and enjoy full independence. 4.4.6 A member of the Board who has, or appears to have, a conflict of interest shall recuse themselves from the case. Where a party to the proceedings requests such recusal, the decision shall be taken by the President of the Board. 4.4.7 In the case where a party to the proceedings requests the recusal of the President of the Board, due to a conflict of interest or the appearance of it, the decision shall be taken by a majority vote of the panel members, excluding the President of the Board who shall have no voting rights. In case of equal votes, recusal of the President will prevail. 4.4.8 In case of misconduct or incapacity, a member of the Board may only be removed by the decision of the GM upon confirmation by the other members of the Board. 4.4.9 A member of the Board may resign by notifying the GM in writing. The resignation shall take effect from the date of notification, unless the notice of resignation specifies a later date. 4.4.10 In case the member of the Board resigning is President or Vice-Preside

The expenses associated with the remuneration of the members of the Board in each appeal shall be borne by the appellant. 1 4.6.2 The combined fees of the Board members deciding on the Appeal in no circumstance can exceed the fees paid by the appellant. 4.6.3 Unless the required fees have been duly received from the appellant, the Secretariat sha

The appeal against debarment of suppliers must be based on one or several of the following grounds: a. NSPA breached the supplier’s procedural right s by failing to give it an opportunity to respond to allegations or by failing to take into account exculpating evidence; b. NSPA made an error of fact in finding that the supplier had engaged in a sanctionable practice (see Paragraph 5.1 of Reference F); c. NSPA made an error of law in determi ning that the alleged conduct qualified as sanctionable practice (see Paragraph 5.1 of Reference F). 4.7.5 The Board shall not be competent to hear appeals: a. on grounds other than those listed in Paragraph 4.7.1 to Paragraph 4.7.4; b. from individuals or entities that did not participate in the competitive solicitation process or, for appeals challenging a sole source determination pursuant to Paragraph 4.7.3, from individuals or entities that did not submit evidence of their capabilities in accordance with Article 6.3 of Reference C; c. from individuals or entities that failed to submit their tender, bid or proposal before the specified closing date (unless the bidder can

Appeals concerning allegations of sanctionable practices pursuant to Paragraph 5.1 of Reference F shall not be receivable unless the Secretariat of the Board receives it within 30 calendar days from the date of the notification of the Competition Advocate’s decision. 4.8.5 The appeal must be accompanied by a proof of payment of applicable fees set out in Appendix II. The Secretariat shall not register appeals that are not accompanied by a proof of payment. All fees paid by appellants are non-refundable. 4.8.6 An appeal must include all relevant documents and written submissions, including: a. the name and status of the appellant; b. the name of the appellant’s authorised representative, if any; c. the decision being challenged, and a summary of the appeal not exceeding two pages; d. any relevant complaints that the appellant has submitted and the results thereof, which shall be accompanied by all underlying procurement-related documents, including the bidding instructions and the appellant’s bid; e. the legal grounds on which the Appeal is based; f. all supporting evidence. 4.8.7 It is the responsibility of the appellant to present a complete case and to substantiate its claims to the extent necessary for the Board to conduct its review. All appeals shall be decided on the basis of the written submissions and evidence provided by the parties. 4.8.8 Appeals that are incomp

All appeals shall be decided on the basis of the written submissions and evidence provided by the parties. 4.8.8 Appeals that are incomplete or unsubstantiated shall be summarily dismissed. The Board shall not request or invite the appellant to supplement or improve its appeal through the submission of additional evidence or arguments that ought to have been provided at the time of filing the appeal. 4.8.9 The Board shall not assume any inquisitorial or investigatory role nor provide guidance to appellants in preparing or completing their submissions. Should the Board decline such a request, NSPA shall retain the opti on to withdraw the evidence in question from the record. 4.8.13 The appeal process usually consists of two submissions (appeal and reply). If needed, the Board may request the parties to file additional submissions (rejoinder and surrejoinder). 4.8.14 In exceptional circumstances, before issuing its decision, the Board may seek through its Secretariat further information, including from persons with technical knowledge, or documents either from the appellant or from the Agency. 4.8.15 Should the Board receive multiple appeals arising from the same procurement procedure, the Board shall determine, at its discretion, the most appropriate manner and order in which to address the individual appeals. In cases of lowest price technically compliant procurements the Competition Advocate shall issue their Second Level review decisions simultaneously. Unless expressly agreed by NSPA, the receipt of more than one appeal arising from the same procurement process shall not impact the applicable timelines for the Board to issue its decision. The appellant(s) shall be informed by NSPA that, in accordance with the principle of award to the lowest-price techni cally compliant offer, a successful appeal may not result in the appellant being awarded the contract. 4.8.16 All matters that are not expressly provided for in these rules shall be dealt with by decision of the Board on the particular appeal. 4.9 Interim Measures 4.9.1 Appeals relating to allegations of unduly restrictive requirements and against Notifications of Planned Sole Source Award do not suspend the continuation of the solicitation process. Nevertheless, NSPA shall extend the clos ing date for submitting tenders or bids by 21 calendar days from the date NSPA has submitted it s reply to allow the Board to review the appeal and make a final decision. 4.9.2 Upon receipt of an appeal relating to a determination of non-compliance, NSPA shall immediately suspend the decision to award the contract until the final determination by the Board. 4.9.3 If the Board does not issue its final decision within 21 calendar days from the dat

Supporting documents must be accompanied by an English translation. The Agency shall not bear any translation costs; c. manifestly unfounded, dilatory, or abusive. 4.10.4. The Board may only extend the appellant ’s deadline to submit an appeal with NSPA’s consent. 4.11 Final Decision of the Board 4.11.1 The Board shall normally issue its final decisions within 21 calendar days from the date of receipt of NSPA's reply, or exceptional ly, seven calendar days from the receipt of the surrejoinder as applicable. Where a decision cannot be issued within the time limits outlined above, the Board shall inform NSPA and the appellant of the reasons for the delay and provide a date on which a decision will be issued. If the Board does not issue its final decision within 21 calendar days from the date on which NSPA has submitted its reply, NSPA may, but has no obligation to, proceed with the contract award. 4.11.2 The Board shall provide written reasons in support of its final decision. The complainant or appellant shall be entitled to receive a copy of the decision within three working days of its release. The Board’s decision shall contain the following sections: overview or summary, concise statement of relevant facts, issues to be determined, analysis, and conclusion. 4.12 Possible Remedies The only remedies that may be awarded by the Board are those listed below. The Board cannot award material, moral, or punitive damages, nor can the Board order a party to compensate the other party’s legal expenses. 4.12.1 If the Board determines tha

The Board cannot award material, moral, or punitive damages, nor can the Board order a party to compensate the other party’s legal expenses. 4.12.1 If the Board determines that the complaint for unduly restrictive competition is well founded, the only remedy it can grant is an order directing NSPA to amend the Request for Proposals by removing unduly restrictive specifications or requirements and to re-advertise the Request for Proposals. 4.12.2 If the Board determines that the complaint for a determination of non-compliance is well founded, the only remedy it can grant is an order directing NSPA to re-evaluate the bid. 4.12.3 If the Board determines that NSPA erred in determining the sole source character of a requirement, the only remedy it can grant is an order directing NSPA to cancel the Notification of Planned Sole Source Awards and issue a competitive RFP. 4.12.4 If the Board determines that the appeal against a debarment determination is well founded, the only remedy it can grant is the supplier’s reinstatement as an eligible supplier. PURPOSE This Operating Instruction (OI) seeks to ensure that sourcing is fully aligned with NSPA’s principles and goals. It sets forth the rules to determine a supplier's eligibility for registration in the NSPA Source File, to receive NSPA solicitations and to submit offers. The OI identifies all NSP A personnel involved in this process and the principles guiding their p erformance to ensure the goods, services and works th e Agency purchases , meet customers ’ requirements in compliance with the applicable policy and ultimately deliver value for money. 2. DEVIATIONS Unless otherwise stated, exceptions to, or deviations from this OI may not be made unless authorised and appro ved on a case - by - case basis by the Competition Advocate (CA) or the General Manager (GM) upon recommendation by the Competition Advocate . 4. DEFINITIONS For the purposes of this Operating Instruction: 4.1 “ Category classification ” means a strategic approach to procurement where organisations target their investment at areas that contain similar or related products enabling focused opportunities for consolidation, efficiency and automation. 4.2 “ Customer ” means the NATO Member N ation or group of Nations (to include Partner Nations when approved by the Council), the NATO resource committee s , the NATO entity (e.g. NATO Command or Agency) or other international entities when approved by the Council that as a budget holder has the authority to obl igate and expend funds. 4.3 “ Debarment ” is a measure that renders a supplier ineligible to participate in NSPA procurements and enter into contracts with or involving NSPA following the determination, by NSPA, that said supplier has

The most common type of e - auction is “reverse auction”. It will ordinarily be assessed based on the place where the most senior person or group of persons makes its decisions, the place where actions to be taken by the entity as a whole is determined, or any other criteria deemed relevant by NSPA. 4.11 “ Reverse auction ” means a type of auction where there are multiple suppliers and one buyer and the sellers aim to outdo their competition by p lacing a lower offer bid for supplies, services or works placed for auction. 4.12 “ Source ” means a supplier who is a prospective bidder or contractor capable of meet ing or deliver ing on a given requirement. 4.13 “ Source File ” is the NSPA database containing the info rmation on registered suppliers or vendors

PRINCIPLES 5.1 Equality of A ccess to Public Procurement and Equal Treatment Sourcing shall be performed to allow for strict compliance with the principles of equality of ac cess to public procurement and the equal treatment of all suppliers in order to enhance the chance of a successful competitive process. 5.2 Transparency Transparency is the guiding principle to ensure that sourcing is performed on behalf of NATO with honesty , compliance and integrity. 5.3 Competition Above the low value threshold (i.e. Financial Level ‘B’), NSPA shall stimulate competition to ensure customers obtain the best solution pursuant to NSPO Procurement Regulations 4200 and the NSPA OI 4200 - 01. 5.4 Effectiveness Sourcing shall facilitate the selection of suppliers through the receipt, retention and reporting of supplier eligibility and performance information . This is a key element in selection of the optimal source and minimises the risks for the

It consolidates r egistration and performance - related information submitted by the Programme Offices and Divisions (POD) throughout the Agency. It conducts category management when appropriate. 5.6 Agility Upon early communication by the POD’s about new potential activities an d sources, while avoiding directed Procurement, Sourcing shall endeavour to make it possible to react quickly to customers' demand, market changes and shorten the lead - time between the requirement formulation and contract award . 5.7 Lean Source identification, assessment and selection shall be conducted by eliminating all non - value - adding activities. REQUIREMENTS FOR REGISTRATION IN THE NSPA SOURCE FILE 8.1 Only sources registered in Source File are authorized to participate in NSPA solicitations , except for P - Card and ‘ one - time vendor’ purchases . 8.2 Companies or entities applying for registration in NSPA Source File and wishing to participate in a procurement solicitation shall meet the requirements set out in the paragraphs below. 8.3 Legal Personality 8.3.1 The applicant has under the legislation of a State the capacity to enter into contracts, acquire and dispose of property, and take legal action. 8.3.2 Evidence of the legal personality (e.g. registration extract, articles of incorporation) is usually required as part of the registrati on process. 8.4 Nationality 8.4.1 In accordance with NSPO Governance (cf. reference 4. 1 ), NSPA’s , Procurement shall normally be limited to firms or governmental services located within N ATO Member Nations. 8.4.2 The nationality of companies or entities applying for registration will be determined based on: 8.4.2.1 Primarily, the country of incorporation or legal residence; and 8.4.2.2 Secondly, the location of the main production facilities and/or effective administration. 8.4.3 Both criteria shall remain within a NATO Member Nation and, preferably , the same Nation. Registration of companies or entities under a NATO Member Nation based on the criterion of incorporation or legal residence while the main production and/or effective administration are located outside a NATO Member Nation woul d factually circumvent the geographical limitation set forth by NSPO regulations and, consequently, will not be accepted. 8.4.4 The NSPO Procurement Regulations also foresee a number of exceptions where contracts may be let to firms in Nations that are not membe rs of NATO. Companies located in non - NATO Member Nations may be registered in Source File when, at the moment of registration, one or more of these exceptions may be applicable to the applicant in relation with an on - going, upcoming or expected requiremen t. DEFINITIONS 4.1 “ Balance of probabilities”, also known as pr eponderance of evidence, is a standard of proof that is met if it is more likely than not that an alleged fact occurred. 4.2 “POD” means NSPA’s Programmes, Offices , and Divisons. 4.3 “Sanctioned supplier ” is a supplier that has been sanctioned for having engaged in a s anctionable p ractice within the meaning of section 5 of this Operating Instruction. 4.4 “Suspension” is a provisional measure, which prevents a supplier from participating in NSPA procurements pending the outc ome of debarment proceedings. 4.5 “ Supplier ” means any legal entity or individual, including their agents or representatives, that do or seek to do business with NSPA. DEBARMENT Debarment is a measure that renders a supplier ineligible to participate in NSPA procurements and enter into contracts with or involving NSPA following the determination, by NSPA, that said supplier has engaged or attempted to engage in a s anctionable p ractice . 5.1 Sanctionable Practices 5.1.1 Practices that are sanctionable under this Operating Instruction include: 5.1.1.1 b reaches of section 4.1 of the NSPA Code of Conduct ; 5.1.1.2 a violation of the oblig ations contained in the NSPA Supplier Code of Conduct ; 5.1.1.3 a cts or omissions by a supplier that may hinder the inves tigations with a view to determine whether a s anctionable p ractice occurred . 5.1.2 Whether a practice is sanctionable does not depend on whether it occurred in connection with a NSPA procurement or contract. 5.2 Attribution of A cts by the Supplier ’s E mployees , A gents or R epresentatives Vendors are deemed to be vicariously liable for sanctionable acts of their employees and agents. 5.3 Cross - Debarment NSPA may implement debarment decisions made by NATO Member Nations , Partner Nations, and other NATO bodies . 5.4 Debarment D ue to a C riminal C onviction A supplier may also be debarred if it has been established by a court of law that said supplier engaged in criminal conduct, even if the conduc

DEBARMENT PROCEEDINGS 6.1 Commencement of Debarment Proceedings Upon receipt of allegations of sanctionable conduct , NSPA sha ll conduct a preliminary review to determine whether the allegations are prima facie credible and warrant an investigation. Where necessary, a n investigator shall be designated to conduct an investigation . The investigator shall indicate whether the allege d s anctionable p ractice ( s ) occurred on b alance of p robabilities. The preliminary review shall not take longer than fifteen (15) NSPA business days. 6.2 Investigation Report Upon completing the investigation, the i nvestigator shall submit , to the Competition Advocate , a n i nvestigation report that

Before making such a determination, the Competition Advocate shall seek advice from the NSPA/NSPO Office of the Legal Advisor , who will recommend an appropriate period of debarment . 6.3.1 If the Competition Advocate dete rmines that the allegations of s anctionable p ractice are not substantiated, they shall discon tin ue the debarment.
